title_es: Auto Scaling y balanceo de carga
body_es: AWS Auto Scaling ajusta automáticamente la capacidad de los recursos en respuesta a la demanda, garantizando disponibilidad y optimizando costos. Para EC2, los Auto Scaling Groups (ASG) definen configuraciones de lanzamiento, capacidad mínima, deseada y máxima. Las políticas de escalado incluyen: Simple Scaling (basada en una alarma de CloudWatch), Step Scaling (escalado proporcional a la magnitud de la alarma), Target Tracking (mantiene una métrica objetivo como CPU al 70%), y Scheduled Scaling para patrones predecibles. AWS proporciona tres tipos de Elastic Load Balancers: ALB (Application Load Balancer) para HTTP/HTTPS con enrutamiento basado en contenido, rutas y cabeceras; NLB (Network Load Balancer) para TCP/UDP de ultra baja latencia con IPs estáticas; y GLB (Gateway Load Balancer) para appliances virtuales de red de terceros. Para el SAA-C03, la integración entre ASG y ALB/NLB es fundamental: el balanceador distribuye tráfico entre instancias saludables y el ASG reemplaza automáticamente las instancias que fallen los health checks. El Scale-In Protection evita que instancias con trabajo en curso sean terminadas prematuramente. Las políticas de Lifecycle Hooks permiten ejecutar acciones personalizadas durante el lanzamiento o terminación de instancias.
body_en: AWS Auto Scaling dynamically adjusts resource capacity in response to changing demand, ensuring both availability and cost efficiency. EC2 Auto Scaling Groups (ASGs) define launch templates, minimum, desired, and maximum capacity. Scaling policies include: Simple Scaling (triggers on a single CloudWatch alarm), Step Scaling (proportional response based on alarm magnitude), Target Tracking (maintains a target metric like 70% average CPU), and Scheduled Scaling for predictable recurring patterns. AWS offers three Elastic Load Balancer types: Application Load Balancer (ALB) operates at Layer 7, supporting content-based routing by path, hostname, and HTTP headers — ideal for microservices; Network Load Balancer (NLB) operates at Layer 4 with ultra-low latency and static IPs, suited for high-performance TCP/UDP workloads; Gateway Load Balancer (GLB) transparently routes traffic through third-party virtual network appliances. ASGs integrate with ALB and NLB for health check-based replacement: unhealthy instances are terminated and replaced automatically. Instance Refresh enables rolling updates to launch templates with configurable minimum healthy percentages. Lifecycle Hooks pause instance launch or termination to run custom scripts, enabling configuration or graceful draining before an instance enters or leaves service.
example_code:
# Create Auto Scaling group
aws autoscaling create-auto-scaling-group \
  --auto-scaling-group-name my-asg \
  --launch-template LaunchTemplateName=my-template \
  --min-size 2 \
  --max-size 10 \
  --desired-capacity 4

# Create scaling policy
aws autoscaling put-scaling-policy \
  --auto-scaling-group-name my-asg \
  --policy-name scale-up \
  --policy-type TargetTrackingScaling \
  --target-tracking-configuration TargetValue=70.0,PredefinedMetricSpecification={PredefinedMetricType=ASGAverageCPUUtilization}
